answer.rationale: The competitor price cut creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, and memory_73 endorses it — but the recovered source exp_73 shows that summary is lossy in exactly the dangerous direction: +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue masked -12% 30-day retention, with the explicit conclusion NOT to generalize discounting as sustainable growth. Since the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching the discount would buy acquisition that dies before first renewal and would worsen the churn problem it is meant to solve. enterprise_sales_assist is the only other memory with a verified source (exp_44), but it is explicitly enterprise-only and even reduces signup — it does nothing for a price-sensitive SMB base under churn pressure. That leaves the value-delivery levers. Two independent memories (31, 86) converge on signup/onboarding simplification lifting activation, completion, and time-to-value, and memory_91 points the same way; strengthening perceived value is the structurally correct answer to a price attack, because it moves the comparison off price. Critically, the exp_73 case proves these archived summaries can omit retention harm, and memory_31/86/91/57 are all unverified single-line consolidations of that same lossy type — memory_31's 'cut required fields' in particular could plausibly degrade lead quality or downstream retention in a way the summary would not have recorded. So I act, but at small_guarded_test scale with retention and qualified-revenue gates instrumented from the start rather than activation alone, and I do not treat the onboarding memories as established. Next cycle's verification budget should go first to memory_31 and memory_86 (the basis of this action), then memory_91 and memory_57; memory_73 should be rewritten in durable memory to carry the retention penalty so no future session repeats the generalization. If leadership needs a same-day answer on price: hold price, respond with value and targeted retention outreach, and revisit only with evidence that survives a renewal cycle.
